data.title: Daiseki Subsidiary Wins Major METI Subsidy for Plastic Recycling Project
data.description:
Daiseki Co ( (JP:9793) ) has shared an announcement.

Daiseki Co., Ltd. said its consolidated subsidiary, Daiseki Eco. Solution Co., Ltd., has been selected to receive a government subsidy under Japan’s Large-Scale Growth Investment Subsidy program, aimed at labor-saving measures and sustainable wage increases for mid-tier and small and medium-sized enterprises. The funded initiative is the Plastic Resource Recycling Project in Shizuoka City, underscoring the group’s commitment to expanding its environmental and recycling footprint.

The project entails an investment of about ¥9.9 billion, with an expected subsidy of roughly ¥2.9 billion, tied to a targeted 10.4% increase in total wage payments per employee involved in the project. Daiseki noted that the subsidy will be booked as extraordinary income in the fiscal year ending February 2030 and will be accompanied by advanced depreciation for tax purposes, while having no impact on previously announced earnings forecasts for the year ending February 2027, signaling limited near-term financial effect but material long-term support for its recycling operations.

data.title: J. Front Retailing Sees PARCO Growth Offset Softer Department Store Sales in August 2026
data.description:
J FRONT RETAILING Co ( (JP:3086) ) has shared an update.

J. Front Retailing reported mixed performance across its segments for August and the first half of fiscal 2026, with total consolidated revenue roughly flat year on year in August and modest growth over the half. Department store gross sales slipped slightly in August, reflecting weaker traffic at key locations such as Daimaru Umeda, while some regional stores including Hakata Daimaru and Daimaru Sapporo posted robust gains.

Category trends at Daimaru Matsuzakaya showed strength in household goods, fine arts and jewelry, and cosmetics, contrasted by declines in men’s clothing, accessories, and restaurant and café sales, underscoring shifting consumer spending patterns. The PARCO shopping center business remained a clear growth driver, with tenant transaction volume up 8.6% in August and 8.9% for the half across most stores and merchandise categories, highlighting the group’s stronger momentum in mall-based and tenant-driven formats versus its more mature department store operations.
